Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading

Second Reading7 April 2026 – 8 April 2026 bill-789, bill-790, bill-791

A Bill at Second Reading that extends Minimum Energy Performance Standards and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use, and empowers the Minister to make regulations for online platforms to remove non-compliant listings.

From 1 July 2026, end users importing regulated goods for their own use are to register with NEA, meet MEPS and carry MELS labels, with fines up to $10,000 per import for non-compliance. Registration and renewal fees for end users are to be waived, and existing schemes such as the Energy Efficiency Grant and Climate Vouchers are cited as support. The Bill excludes second-hand or used regulated goods and regulated lamps.

What happens next The Senior Minister of State said the new regulations are intended to take effect from 1 July 2026; the transcript does not record a vote or later stage.

Open questions from this debate (19)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • How many regulated goods are currently imported for own use, and what is their total annual energy consumption?
  • What is the projected reduction in energy consumption if all F&B businesses deploy MEPS- and MELS-compliant appliances?
  • How will NEA enforce the requirement for goods arriving by post, courier, land checkpoints, or checked baggage?
  • Will there be a transition period or fee support for SMEs, consumers and first-time applicants?
  • How will the Bill treat individuals who later sell an imported appliance on peer-to-peer platforms?
  • Will software-driven energy degradation after registration be regulated, and how?
  • Will lighting be included in the own-use import regime, and on what timeline?
  • Will waivers and Director-General decisions be published or reported in aggregated form?
  • Will online platforms be required to screen listings before they appear, and what consumer protections apply after payment?
  • Will the Energy Efficiency Grant be expanded to cover all regulated goods?
  • Will there be top-ups to the Climate Friendly Households Programme for lower-income families?
  • Will there be a shared product registry or simplified pathway for subsequent importers?
  • Will there be an interagency coordination framework and a single point of contact for importers?
  • Will there be public reporting to Parliament on waivers, appeals and enforcement trends?
  • Will there be a priority processing lane for SMEs with high-efficiency products?
  • What is the projected cost impact on households and SMEs?
  • Will compliant models remain competitively priced?
  • How will NEA distinguish deliberate circumvention from genuine misunderstanding?
  • Will registration of goods be retrospectively revoked if a software update degrades performance?

Ministerial statements on the Middle East conflict and support measures for Singapore

7 April 2026 ministerial-statement-2952

A series of ministerial statements addressing parliamentary questions on the impact of the Middle East situation on Singapore, followed by grouped clarifications from ministers.

The statements set out support measures including $200 cash for active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month; enhanced U-Save rebates; $500 CDC vouchers brought forward to June 2026; and a $200 increase to the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment, with about 2.4 million Singaporeans receiving cash in September. They also state that the regulated electricity tariff is expected to rise more sharply in the next adjustment and that overall inflation for 2026 is expected to be higher than earlier projected.

  • Mr Gan Kim Yong

    • The conflict has entered its sixth week and Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, with vessel traffic falling sharply.

      Verbatim23 words
      Last month, only about six vessels on average passed through the Strait of Hormuz each day, compared to around 135 in normal times.

    • Brent crude oil prices doubled from just before the conflict to a peak.

      Verbatim25 words
      Since the onset of the conflict, Brent crude oil prices have doubled from US$71 per barrel just before the conflict, to a peak of US$141.

    • The Government convened the Homefront Crisis Ministerial Committee, chaired by Mr K Shanmugam.

      Verbatim25 words
      This is why we have convened the Homefront Crisis Ministerial Committee (HCMC), chaired by Coordinating Minister for National Security K Shanmugam and comprising several Ministers.

    • The regulated electricity tariff increased by 2.1% to about 27.27 cents per kWh for the second quarter of 2026.

      Verbatim26 words
      The regulated electricity tariff, which most Singapore households pay, increased by 2.1% to about 27.27 cents per kilowatt hour (kWh) for the second quarter of 2026.

    • Overall inflation for 2026 is now expected to be higher than earlier projected.

      Verbatim15 words
      Consequently, we now expect Singapore's overall inflation for 2026 to be higher than earlier projected.

    • MAS will release its upcoming assessment of the inflation outlook on 14 April 2026.

      Verbatim23 words

What happens next MAS will release its inflation outlook on 14 April 2026; MTI will update the GDP forecast in May; BCA will issue a circular shortly; the Government will seek Parliament's approval for a supplementary budget later; the HCMC will continue to monitor the situation. The Sitting was suspended until 5.30 pm.

Adjournment motion on return-to-work support for injured and ill workers

Motion to adjourn7 April 2026 matter-adj-2955

An adjournment motion in which Mr Melvin Yong spoke on strengthening return-to-work support for injured and ill workers, and the Minister of State for Manpower responded.

The transcript records proposals to strengthen return-to-work support and a planned MOM review, but it does not state any immediate change to entitlements or support for workers. MOM says it will launch an Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity in the second half of 2026. The record does not set out the practical impact of these steps.

  • Ms Indranee Rajah

    • Ms Indranee Rajah moved that Parliament adjourn.

      Verbatim5 words
      That Parliament do now adjourn.

  • Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)

    • Mr Melvin Yong said Singapore recorded 660 major workplace injuries in 2025.

      Verbatim8 words
      In 2025, Singapore recorded 660 major workplace injuries.

    • Mr Melvin Yong said return-to-work must be treated as a core pillar of the workforce system.

      Verbatim16 words
      return-to-work must be treated as a core pillar of our workforce system, not a secondary consideration.

    • Mr Melvin Yong said leading jurisdictions share three principles: early intervention, shared responsibility and workplace-centred solutions.

      Verbatim14 words
      Across these systems, three principles stand out: early intervention, shared responsibility and workplace-centred solutions.

    • Mr Melvin Yong proposed strengthening early intervention through earlier referral, clearer employer expectations and early coordination.

      Verbatim30 words
      We should therefore strengthen early intervention by encouraging earlier referral into return-to-work support; establishing clearer expectations for employer engagement; and promoting early coordination between employers, workers, insurers and healthcare practitioners.

    • Mr Melvin Yong said the forthcoming Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity intends to explore industry-led solutions to promote return-to-work.

      Verbatim25 words

What happens next Parliament adjourned at 7.37 pm. The next sitting is tomorrow at 12.00 pm. MOM will conduct a review of the return-to-work landscape, and will launch the Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity with NTUC and SNEF in the second half of 2026; the public is encouraged to participate in ground-up solutions later in the year.
